entries.action: Use complete ARRAY_PARTITION on the small local dimension that maps to concurrent lane reads.
contraindications: Do not complete-partition large external arrays.
Do not partition a dimension not used by the concurrent accesses.
entries.expected_signal: The lane loop reaches lower II with bounded register growth.
preconditions: A small local array is indexed with parallel lane accesses.
Complete banking is within LUT/FF budget.

entries.action: Prefer cyclic ARRAY_PARTITION when strided lane accesses need distinct banks.
contraindications: Do not use cyclic banking for contiguous packed-word bandwidth.
Do not choose a factor unrelated to the lane/stride pattern.
entries.expected_signal: Bank conflicts fall and achieved II improves on the measured loop.
preconditions: Accesses are strided across a known dimension.
The modulo pattern maps lanes across banks.

entries.action: Apply ARRAY_PARTITION to the measured array and access dimension, using the minimum factor that can satisfy the required ports.
contraindications: Do not partition unrelated top-level arrays speculatively.
Do not combine ARRAY_PARTITION and ARRAY_RESHAPE on the same variable.
Over-partitioning can increase LUT, FF, and BRAM disproportionately.
entries.expected_signal: The memory-port II lower bound falls and achieved II improves.
preconditions: Synthesis identifies parallel accesses or a memory-port II lower bound on a named array.
The contended array dimension and required access factor are known.

entries.action: Apply ARRAY_RESHAPE to the adjacent access dimension with a width/factor justified by the consumer lanes.
contraindications: Do not use reshape for irregular or independent-bank access.
Do not combine ARRAY_RESHAPE and ARRAY_PARTITION on the same variable.
entries.expected_signal: Useful bandwidth per access increases without unnecessary bank replication.
preconditions: Adjacent elements are consumed together.
The limiting evidence is storage or interface word width rather than independent-bank access.

entries.action: Choose either ARRAY_RESHAPE for packed adjacent bandwidth or ARRAY_PARTITION for independent banks, not both on the same variable.
contraindications: Do not stack storage directives to guess around an II issue.
Do not reshape irregular access patterns.
entries.expected_signal: The directive set remains explainable and avoids redundant storage expansion.
preconditions: A candidate proposes both reshape and partition on the same variable.
The access pattern is not independently proven for both.

entries.action: Keep top-level interface widths stable; narrow only internal temporaries unless the contract allows an ABI change.
contraindications: Do not change top argument types in optimize mode.
Do not break m_axi word alignment.
entries.expected_signal: Interface validation remains pass while internal resource use can improve.
preconditions: A type-width change touches top-level ports.
The testbench or host interface expects a fixed ABI.

entries.action: Narrow bitwidth only when range and quantization behavior are explicit in source or task contract.
contraindications: Do not infer a narrower type from one test vector.
Do not change saturation or rounding semantics silently.
entries.expected_signal: DSP/LUT/FF use falls without public CSim mismatch.
preconditions: The source uses ap_int or ap_fixed.
Value range or error budget is known.

entries.action: For byte-oriented crypto kernels, improve one measured round component at a time: pipeline the dominant bounded loop or partition only the small lookup/state array that supplies concurrent byte lanes.
contraindications: Do not fully unroll all encryption rounds without clock and resource evidence.
Do not replace arithmetic S-box or Galois-field logic with an unverified lookup table.
Do not change byte ordering, key schedule semantics, or top-level buffers.
entries.expected_signal: The selected round or substitution loop improves latency or II while preserving clock and avoiding broad LUT/FF growth.
preconditions: The kernel is byte-oriented crypto or substitution logic such as AES, DES, S-box, XOR rounds, or Galois-field byte transforms.
A small state, key, or lookup-like array is the local source of parallel byte accesses.
Synthesis evidence identifies a single bounded loop or helper as the next optimization target.

entries.action: Set an evidence-based explicit channel depth and verify backpressure, stall behavior, and required CoSim.
contraindications: Do not use a very large depth to hide an architectural ordering bug.
Do not claim deadlock safety from C simulation.
entries.expected_signal: Required CoSim completes without deadlock while FIFO resources remain bounded.
preconditions: Producer and consumer rates or burst sizes can differ.
The channel is an hls::stream or equivalent bounded FIFO.

entries.action: Do not add DATAFLOW until producer/consumer ownership is separated by streams or clearly single-writer buffers.
contraindications: Do not rely on CSim to prove task-level scheduling safety.
Do not split functions that share hidden global state.
entries.expected_signal: Avoids synthesis or CoSim failures from ambiguous shared mutation.
preconditions: A DATAFLOW region has shared arrays or globals between stages.
Stage ownership is ambiguous.

entries.action: Tune DATAFLOW only when a DATAFLOW region and explicit stage boundaries already exist. Do not introduce a new task graph in this phase; every change requires real CoSim.
contraindications: Do not introduce DATAFLOW into shared mutable state or ambiguous stage ownership.
C simulation alone cannot prove bounded FIFO behavior or absence of RTL deadlock.
entries.expected_signal: Stage execution overlaps and throughput approaches the slowest stage interval.
preconditions: The kernel has clear producer, compute, and consumer stages.
Channel ownership and bounded producer/consumer behavior are explicit.

entries.action: Diagnose the compile-stage error before proposing any QoR optimization.
contraindications: Do not accept a QoR claim from a compile-failing candidate.
Do not inspect hidden or evaluator artifacts for the fix.
entries.expected_signal: The next candidate restores CSim/Synth pass before Q_HW selection.
preconditions: A candidate fails CSim compile or synthesis compile.
The previous best was valid.

entries.action: Record the action as a negative case and choose a different measured bottleneck rather than repeating it.
contraindications: Do not ban the whole optimization family.
Only reject the measured action under compatible structure and target.
entries.expected_signal: Subsequent retrieval avoids wasting API tokens on repeated no-op changes.
preconditions: A candidate preserves public correctness but Q_HW does not improve.
The action contract is no-op or unrelated to the bottleneck.

entries.action: Compare clock-adjusted latency and worst-resource growth before accepting additional MAC lanes.
contraindications: Do not accept a lower cycle count with severe clock degradation.
Do not exceed DSP headroom.
entries.expected_signal: Q_HW improves rather than cycle latency alone.
preconditions: A GEMM candidate increases DSP parallelism.
Estimated clock or DSP use worsens.

entries.action: Bank only the local tile dimension that is read concurrently by the unrolled compute lanes.
contraindications: Do not complete-partition full matrices.
Do not change tile shape without measuring memory and DSP pressure.
entries.expected_signal: Compute-lane II improves without partitioning unrelated matrices.
preconditions: A GEMM-style kernel reuses local tiles.
The proposed partition targets the accumulation or lane dimension.

entries.action: Preserve the existing blocked/tiled GEMM architecture and local reuse. If the source already has local tiles, keep the tile shape and try only one small loop-local UNROLL factor=2; add minimum banking only on the local tile dimension that feeds concurrent K/lane reads. Do not regress to a scalar fallback or introduce unrelated new tiles/buffers in this phase.
contraindications: Do not copy template interfaces or fixed tile sizes into an existing kernel.
Do not partition tiles without a visible reuse and access-dimension argument.
Do not remove existing blocked/local-buffer reuse just to make the prompt simpler.
entries.expected_signal: External accesses per MAC fall and compute parallelism improves effective latency within resource limits.
preconditions: The source has matrix-multiply-style nested loops.
Tile shape, layout, accumulator type, and local reuse are explicit.
The local tile dimension that supplies concurrent K/lane reads is identifiable before banking.

entries.action: For triangular matrix factorization, preserve row/column dependency order. If baseline synthesis already reports floating-point carried-dependence loops with II around 8-12 and high DSP/LUT pressure, first measure a conservative outer-loop PIPELINE with an II near the reported dependency II before trying II=1 or loop flattening. Otherwise optimize one inner accumulation or update loop at a time with measured pipeline or small-dimension partitioning.
contraindications: Do not interchange or flatten loops across triangular data dependencies unless dependence evidence proves it safe.
Do not fully partition the whole matrix when only one row, column, or local accumulation window needs ports.
Do not change floating-point operation order aggressively unless the task contract allows numeric drift.
Do not force II=1 on floating-point triangular update loops when the report shows dependency-limited II near 10; this often trades a small latency gain for a frequency failure.
entries.expected_signal: The selected triangular update, accumulation, or conservative outer-loop pipeline improves Q_HW by reducing latency or floating-point resource replication without changing factorization semantics or causing broad matrix storage growth.
preconditions: The kernel performs matrix factorization or triangular solve/decomposition such as Cholesky or LU.
The algorithm has loop-carried dependencies across rows, columns, or diagonal updates.
Synthesis evidence identifies a bounded inner accumulation/update loop or a small local matrix dimension.

entries.action: Inline only the measured hotspot helper, then synthesize to verify schedule and resource effects.
contraindications: Do not recursively inline a whole helper tree.
Do not inline large functions that hide memory stages.
entries.expected_signal: Function overhead or scheduling barriers fall without widespread code growth.
preconditions: A small helper function is on the measured critical path.
Inlining exposes pipeline or constant-propagation opportunities.

entries.action: Keep m_axi depth concrete and consistent with public testbench allocation.
contraindications: Do not delete depth metadata to simplify pragmas.
Do not use a depth smaller than the public test extent.
entries.expected_signal: Interface checks and CoSim memory modeling remain valid.
preconditions: A top-level pointer or m_axi interface is present.
C/RTL co-simulation or host modeling needs bounded memory.

entries.action: Keep scalar controls and return on s_axilite unless the task explicitly requires another control protocol.
contraindications: Do not switch ap_ctrl_none on a transactional kernel.
Do not alter top-level ABI in optimize mode.
entries.expected_signal: Interface validation remains stable while internal QoR changes are isolated.
preconditions: The kernel uses accelerator-style top-level control.
Scalar control arguments are present.

entries.action: Split the loop only when stage boundaries and storage ownership are explicit.
contraindications: Do not split loops with ambiguous dependencies.
Do not duplicate memory traffic while chasing parallelism.
entries.expected_signal: The bottleneck stage becomes independently pipelinable or dataflow-capable.
preconditions: One loop mixes memory movement and compute.
Separate stages can communicate through a bounded buffer or stream.

entries.action: Apply LOOP_FLATTEN only to a compatible nest with proven bounds and no intervening side effects.
contraindications: Do not flatten imperfect nests with boundary code.
Do not flatten when dependence analysis is uncertain.
entries.expected_signal: Loop overhead or scheduling interval improves without functional changes.
preconditions: A nested loop is perfect or semi-perfect.
Flattening does not change loop-carried state semantics.

entries.action: Fuse adjacent passes only when it reduces memory traffic without worsening II.
contraindications: Do not fuse loops with conflicting pipeline schedules.
Do not fuse when it creates additional live-range pressure.
entries.expected_signal: Latency or memory transactions fall while achieved II remains stable.
preconditions: Adjacent loops traverse the same bounded range.
Fusion does not increase recurrence or memory-port conflicts.

entries.action: Add LOOP_TRIPCOUNT only as reporting guidance; do not treat it as a performance optimization by itself.
contraindications: Do not count tripcount annotation as Q_HW improvement.
Do not invent bounds not present in source or task contract.
entries.expected_signal: Reports become more interpretable while synthesized hardware behavior remains unchanged.
preconditions: A loop bound is data-dependent but bounded by task constants.
The report lacks useful latency estimates.

entries.action: Use CORDIC-specific structure only for confirmed CORDIC intent; otherwise preserve existing math code.
contraindications: Do not introduce CORDIC for unrelated bit rotations.
Do not change numeric scale without a contract.
entries.expected_signal: DSP/latency tradeoff improves for the intended transform family.
preconditions: The confirmed design intent is trigonometric or vector rotation.
CORDIC numeric format and iteration count are explicit.

entries.action: Exploit FIR symmetry or specialized structure only when coefficients and sample ordering prove it.
contraindications: Do not assume coefficient symmetry.
Do not change sample phase or decimator schedule.
entries.expected_signal: Multiplier count or latency improves with identical public output.
preconditions: The kernel is a FIR filter.
Coefficients are symmetric or decimation/interpolation intent is explicit.

entries.action: Enable unsafe math or algebraic reassociation only when explicitly allowed and validated against tolerance.
contraindications: Do not assume unsafe math for sensitive kernels.
Do not change NaN, rounding, or exception-sensitive behavior silently.
entries.expected_signal: Latency or DSP use improves while CSim remains within tolerance.
preconditions: The kernel uses floating-point math or transcendental operations.
The task contract allows approximate numerical behavior.

entries.action: Assign independent m_axi ports to distinct bundle names when concurrent bandwidth is required.
contraindications: Do not split bundles for intentionally shared arbitration.
Keep depth concrete for C/RTL co-simulation.
entries.expected_signal: Interface arbitration pressure falls and memory throughput improves.
preconditions: Independent external memories are read or written concurrently.
The top-level interface uses m_axi ports.

entries.action: Prefer explicit local buffering for reuse before increasing external memory ports.
contraindications: Do not introduce a buffer without a reuse story.
Do not change output ordering or boundary behavior.
entries.expected_signal: External memory transactions per operation fall and local storage growth is bounded.
preconditions: The kernel repeatedly accesses external memory.
A local reuse window or tile is visible.

entries.action: Apply PIPELINE to the throughput-controlling scope with a report-supported II target.
contraindications: Outer-loop pipelining may force inner-loop concurrency and expose memory-port pressure.
Do not add PIPELINE when the measured loop is already II=1 and latency is trip-count dominated.
entries.expected_signal: Loop interval or function throughput improves while timing and resource capacity remain valid.
preconditions: A specific loop or function scope controls throughput.
Loop structure and current achieved II are known.

entries.action: Model the implied inner-loop concurrency before outer-loop PIPELINE; add banking only when the accessed dimension proves it.
contraindications: Do not treat outer PIPELINE as a syntax-only change.
Do not guess partition dimension or factor.
entries.expected_signal: Outer-loop throughput improves without unresolved port conflicts or uncontrolled resource replication.
preconditions: An outer loop is considered for pipelining.
Inner-loop access concurrency and memory ports can be inspected.

entries.action: Pipeline the outer loop only when the report and source prove inner-loop concurrency is intended and memory ports can support it.
contraindications: Do not pipeline an outer loop as a default latency fix.
Avoid this when inner loops have variable bounds or shared mutable state.
entries.expected_signal: Function interval improves without new memory-port II warnings or large resource growth.
preconditions: An outer loop controls throughput.
Inner loops or memory accesses may become concurrent.

entries.action: Use PIPELINE rewind only for a valid continuous loop pipeline whose state behavior remains correct across transactions.
contraindications: Do not use rewind to mask a deadlock.
Do not use rewind on a loop with invalid persistent state semantics.
entries.expected_signal: Back-to-back interval improves while CSim and required CoSim preserve transaction behavior.
preconditions: A loop pipeline handles back-to-back transactions.
State carried between loop invocations is understood.

entries.action: For a statically bounded associative integer reduction, first try only a loop-local partial UNROLL factor=2; preserve the accumulator and numeric contract. Do not introduce a new tree architecture in this phase.
contraindications: Do not restructure non-associative floating-point operations without permission.
Unrolling without an accumulator policy can hide overflow and timing risk.
entries.expected_signal: The loop-carried accumulation path shortens and effective latency improves at acceptable area cost.
preconditions: The dominant computation is an associative reduction.
The operator, accumulator type, numerical behavior, and desired tree shape are explicit.

entries.action: Preserve floating-point associativity semantics unless the task contract allows numerical differences.
contraindications: Do not build a tree for bit-exact floating-point code without permission.
Do not enable unsafe math silently.
entries.expected_signal: CSim remains stable under the public tolerance and timing does not regress.
preconditions: The reduction uses floating-point arithmetic.
A candidate changes operation order.

entries.action: Use a small number of independent accumulators before a final combine, then measure Q_HW.
contraindications: Do not change overflow semantics.
Do not over-unroll beyond measured resource headroom.
entries.expected_signal: Recurrence pressure falls and effective latency improves within area limits.
preconditions: An integer associative reduction has a fixed trip count.
Resource headroom supports multiple accumulators.

entries.action: Choose one measurable bottleneck and change only one optimization class before re-synthesizing.
contraindications: Do not stack directives on an unverified baseline.
Remove or revise a directive that does not improve the limiting metric.
entries.expected_signal: The limiting report metric improves and the effect is attributable to the selected action.
preconditions: A functionally correct C-simulation baseline exists.
A real synthesis report provides latency, clock, loop, and resource evidence.

entries.action: Compare max(target_clock, estimated_clock) times latency before accepting the candidate.
contraindications: Do not use cycles alone as acceptance evidence.
Do not ignore frequency gate failures.
entries.expected_signal: Candidates with lower cycles but worse actual time are rejected.
preconditions: A candidate improves cycle latency but worsens estimated clock.
The scoring target uses hardware time or Q_HW.

entries.action: Classify the II blocker first. If the exact array/recurrence/timing cause is absent, return the kernel unchanged; never add a standalone PIPELINE directive as an II fix.
contraindications: Do not infer memory pressure from top interval alone.
Do not add another PIPELINE directive without matching the measured blocker.
entries.expected_signal: Achieved II moves toward target II without disproportionate worst-resource growth.
preconditions: The synthesis report shows achieved II above the target.
The blocker can be classified from timing, recurrence, memory-port, or interface evidence.

entries.action: Apply at most one optimization family per candidate and measure before asking for another candidate.
contraindications: Do not stack pipeline, unroll, partition, and dataflow in one unmeasured edit.
Do not repeat rejected actions from history.
entries.expected_signal: Token and synthesis budget are spent on attributable changes.
preconditions: Token budget or credit budget is constrained.
Multiple speculative actions are possible.

entries.action: Preserve the top function signature, header contract, and public testbench-visible behavior during any source restructure.
contraindications: Do not change top arguments or header APIs.
Do not import reference or evaluator-only code.
entries.expected_signal: Interface and CSim gates remain pass while QoR evidence changes.
preconditions: A candidate restructures source around helper functions or local buffers.
The task is optimize mode with fixed public TB.

entries.action: Preserve the existing border policy exactly when introducing window or line-buffer optimizations.
contraindications: Do not skip border elements for throughput.
Do not change padding, clamp, or zero-fill behavior silently.
entries.expected_signal: Public CSim remains bit-equivalent while memory reuse improves.
preconditions: A stencil kernel handles image/grid borders.
The candidate changes buffering or loop order.

entries.action: Preserve the existing stencil architecture and boundary behavior. First try only a small UNROLL factor=2 on a statically bounded filter loop; do not introduce a new line buffer in this phase.
contraindications: Do not change the boundary policy.
Do not apply both partition and reshape to the same line buffer.
entries.expected_signal: Memory traffic falls and the stencil loop sustains a lower interval.
preconditions: The source performs repeated neighborhood access over a 2D or 3D grid.
Window shape, boundary policy, and reuse distance are known.

entries.action: Use a shift-register style local window before larger line-buffer restructuring.
contraindications: Do not use for large 2D images without a line-buffer plan.
Do not alter warm-up or boundary behavior.
entries.expected_signal: Repeated loads fall and loop II improves with small FF/LUT growth.
preconditions: The stencil has a small fixed 1D window.
Neighbor reuse is local and bounded.

entries.action: Preserve side-channel fields and TLAST policy when optimizing stream loops.
contraindications: Do not drop side-channel fields during type simplification.
Do not change TLAST generation without a matching interface contract.
entries.expected_signal: CSim and required CoSim preserve packet framing while throughput improves.
preconditions: The interface uses AXIS side channels or TLAST.
The testbench expects frame boundaries.

entries.action: Set stream depth from the measured burst/rate mismatch instead of using an arbitrary large FIFO.
contraindications: Do not hide ordering bugs with large depths.
Do not tune FIFO depth without a DATAFLOW or stream boundary.
entries.expected_signal: Required CoSim passes and FIFO resource use remains bounded.
preconditions: Producer and consumer burst sizes differ.
The FIFO is explicit in source or report evidence.

entries.action: Try one loop-local partial UNROLL with the smallest useful factor, then measure latency, clock, and worst-resource growth.
contraindications: Do not fully unroll a long or dynamically bounded loop.
Do not increase a factor after measured resource growth outweighed speedup.
entries.expected_signal: Effective latency improves more than the worst proportional resource growth.
preconditions: A statically bounded loop dominates latency.
The loop is already pipelined effectively or exposes independent iterations.
Resource headroom is available.

entries.action: Stop increasing the unroll factor once worst-resource growth exceeds effective latency improvement.
contraindications: Do not compare cycle latency alone.
Do not extrapolate from one target part to another.
entries.expected_signal: Candidate selection avoids Q_HW regressions from area-dominated unrolls.
preconditions: A prior unroll factor was measured.
The next factor would increase replicated operators or banks.

entries.action: Avoid unrolling dynamic-bound loops unless a fixed upper bound and validation budget are explicit.
contraindications: Do not full-unroll a data-dependent loop.
Do not invent trip counts absent from source or report evidence.
entries.expected_signal: Synthesis avoids capacity blowups and unsupported full-unroll behavior.
preconditions: A loop has a dynamic or unproven trip count.
The candidate proposes loop unrolling.
